title: SILK: Preventing Latency Spikes in Log-Structured Merge Key-Value Stores
authors: Oana Balmau; Florin Dinu; Willy Zwaenepoel; Karan Gupta; Ravishankar Chandhiramoorthi; Diego Didona
problem: Tail latency in LSM stores caused by interference between client writes, flushes and compactions
mechanism: I/O scheduler: give internal ops more bandwidth when client load is low; prioritize flushes and low-level compactions; preempt compactions
methodology: Implemented in an open-source store derived from RocksDB; compared against RocksDB and TRIAD
datasets_workloads: A production workload from Nutanix plus synthetic benchmarks (further detail not on the abstract page)
results: Up to two orders of magnitude lower p99 latency with no significant harm to other metrics (as stated by the authors)
limitations: Not stated on the abstract page; full paper not read
relation_to_helios: Closest single-node analogue of what the pressure loop tries to do. Its control signal is client load, Helios's is replication state.
potential_gap: Whether a replication-state signal carries information a local client-load signal does not
verification: abstract page read (usenix.org); full paper not read

title: ADOC: Automatically Harmonizing Dataflow Between Components in Log-Structured Key-Value Stores for Improved Performance
authors: Jinghuan Yu; Sam H. Noh; Young-ri Choi; Chun Jason Xue
problem: Write stalls in LSM stores; authors argue they come from data overflowing a component faster than it drains
mechanism: Automatic tuning of RocksDB thread count and batch size to balance data flow between components
methodology: Implemented on RocksDB; evaluated on several storage devices
results: Write-stall duration down by up to 87.9%; up to 322.8% better than auto-tuned RocksDB; up to 66% more throughput than SILK on the synthetic workload, comparable on YCSB; SILK used over 20% more DRAM on average
limitations: Not stated on the abstract page; full paper not read
relation_to_helios: Gives a data-flow framing (backlog growth rate vs drain rate) that maps to apply backlog on a replica
potential_gap: Apply-side backlog across a replication boundary is not covered by single-node data-flow control
verification: abstract page read (usenix.org); full paper not read

title: Perseus: A Fail-Slow Detection Framework for Cloud Storage Systems
authors: Ruiming Lu; Erci Xu; Yiming Zhang; Fengyi Zhu; Zhaosheng Zhu; Mengtian Wang; Zongpeng Zhu; Guangtao Xue; Jiwu Shu; Minglu Li; Jiesheng Wu
problem: Fail-slow storage devices keep running at degraded speed and are hard to detect
mechanism: Lightweight regression-based model for per-drive fail-slow detection and analysis
methodology: Monitored 248K drives in production for 10 months; released a dataset of about 41K normal and 315 verified fail-slow drives; root-cause analysis
baselines: Not stated on the abstract page
results: Found 304 fail-slow cases; isolating detected drives cut node-level 99.99th-percentile tail latency by 48%
limitations: Drive-level detection only; baselines not listed on the page
relation_to_helios: Evidence that slow disks occur at production scale and matter for tails; provides a public dataset that could parametrize fault injection
potential_gap: Detection is per drive. Whether a replicated state machine should react at the protocol level is separate
verification: abstract page read (usenix.org); full paper not read

title: Tolerating Slowdowns in Replicated State Machines using Copilots
authors: Khiem Ngo; Siddhartha Sen; Wyatt Lloyd
problem: Replicated state machines slowed by replicas that are slow but not failed; single-leader designs route work through one replica and detection-based fixes react slowly
mechanism: Two distinguished replicas (pilot and copilot) both order and execute every command; fast takeover with a 10 ms timeout; ping-pong batching; null dependency elimination
methodology: Implemented in Go on the EPaxos framework; slowdowns injected as pauses or added network delay
datasets_workloads: Emulab, 5 replicas in one datacenter (about 0.1 ms RTT), 8-byte commands, closed-loop clients at about 50% of peak load
baselines: Multi-Paxos; EPaxos (0%, 25%, 100% conflict); Fast-View-Change (idealized Multi-Paxos with 10 ms view-change timeout)
results: With one slow replica, worst-case median, p90 and p99 latencies stayed within 0.6, 2 and 4 ms of the no-slowdown values; about 8% to 13% lower throughput than Multi-Paxos when nothing is slow
limitations: Tolerates one slow replica; crash faults only; single datacenter, 5 replicas, simple workload; depends on tuned timeouts; slowdowns were injected, not observed
relation_to_helios: Shows the slow-leader and slow-replica effect on Multi-Paxos and the cost of designing around it. Raft is not evaluated.
potential_gap: Its slowdowns are pauses and network delay. Storage-engine-induced slowness (compaction) is not modelled
verification: fetched PDF summary (princeton.edu); full paper not independently re-read

title: ACaZoo: A Distributed Key-Value Store based on Replicated LSM-Trees
authors: Panagiotis Garefalakis; Panagiotis Papadopoulos; Kostas Magoutis
venue_year: SRDS 2014 (inferred: ERCIM lists it under 2014 publications and the author's PDF is named srds14.pdf; the venue page itself was not read)
problem: LSM compaction at a primary-backup master drains CPU and I/O and degrades throughput
mechanism: Intercepts compaction at the replica-group leader; before compacting, runs a leader election so a non-compacting node takes over; weighted by pending compaction work
methodology: Built on Cassandra with ZooKeeper coordination
datasets_workloads: YCSB 0.1.4, 1 KB records, Zipf and uniform, 100% read / 50-50 / 100% write, 64 or 256 threads, about 1 GB database, 2-vCPU VMs with 20 GB remote disks
baselines: Oracle NoSQL Database 2.1.54; Cassandra Quorum; Cassandra Serial
results: Leader changes raised write-heavy throughput by up to 40% (batch) and 33% (periodic); mixed workloads 20% to 25%
limitations: Helps less when a quorum compacts simultaneously (measured about 23% of the time with 3 nodes, 13% with 5, under 12% with 7); election costs about 100 ms unavailability; cold cache on the new leader; small 3-node groups on CPU-bound VMs
relation_to_helios: Closest prior art for coordinating compaction across replicas. Primary-backup rather than Raft, and compaction on independent nodes
potential_gap: In a deterministic replicated state machine all replicas see the same log, so compaction may be synchronized by construction. Whether that matters under quorum commit is untested
